text:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: Paging: streaming/v1 p99 latency breach (>= 2.5s) detected in region us-west-2. AlertID: INC-2298765. Auto-escalation to on-call.

olivia (oncall): Acked. I'm on it. Initial checks: is this a single node or cluster-wide?

sam (runtime): Seeing a big tail spike on streaming sessions starting ~2298765300. p95 ~450ms, p99 ~2.9s for the last 10m. Throughput steady.

maria (infra): GPU telemetry shows correctable ECC errors rising on gw-node-07 and gpu-temp on that host is ~86C, fan rpm lower than expected. Other nodes show small bumps.

leo (sre): Is there any streaming stall pattern in logs? Could be KV cache thrash or NVMe paging.

sam (runtime): Logs show repeated stalls in the chunked stream writer: many `send_chunk()` calls blocked for >500ms. Stacktrace points to `device_sync` delays.

asha (eng-runtime): Reproduced locally: when ECC correctables spike, the driver does more internal retries -> stalls. Noticed `GPU_PAGE_FAULT` messages in dmesg on gw-node-07.

olivia (oncall): OK. Customer impact? Any 5xx or just slow responses?

jordan (prod): Error rate up for streaming clients using long sessions. ~0.6% 5xx increase (mainly upstream timeouts). Looks like ~12 active customers hit p99 > 2s in last 20m. No auth failures or data errors reported.

olivia (oncall): Good. Priority: mitigate customer impact ASAP with minimal blast radius. Maria, can you cordon/drain gw-node-07? We'll fail traffic to spare capacity.

maria (infra): Starting drain. `kubectl cordon gw-node-07 && kubectl drain gw-node-07 --ignore-daemonsets --delete-emptydir-data --timeout=5m`

incident-bot: Drain job started for gw-node-07. Notifying autoscaler.

sam (runtime): Re-routed 40% of new streams off gw-node-07 via router policy. Monitoring p99.

leo (sre): Quick health check: run `nvidia-smi -q -d ECC` and `dmesg | grep -i -E "ecc|page_fault|thermal"` on gw-node-07.

maria (infra): Ran checks: `nvidia-smi -q -d ECC` shows growing counts for corrected errors. `dmesg` contains repeated `NVRM: GPU has fallen off the bus` transient messages and `thermal event` entries.

asha (eng-runtime): Suggest immediate mitigation: 1) Drain node (in progress) 2) Apply routing fallback for streaming to smaller model variant for affected customers to reduce kernel stress 3) If necessary, spin replacement node.

olivia (oncall): Agreed. Sam, prepare rollout to smaller model variant for the affected customer cohort. Use canary and 5-minute observation.

sam (runtime): Canary config: `route: streaming/v1 -> model: small-llama-7b-quant (canary=10%)`. Applying now.

pagerduty-bot: @olivia Paging: Maria responded to incident.

jordan (prod): Notifying CS to proactively message customers experiencing >=2s p99. No phone pages yet but email batch ready.

olivia (oncall): Any signs of NVLink or PCIe errors? Could be hardware flake.

maria (infra): NVLink counters nominal. PCIe logs show occasional `AER` corrected errors on slot 3. Fan controller firmware shows a slightly older revision.

leo (sre): If ECC correctables continue to increase after drain, we should mark the card for RMA. For now, draining should reduce load. Also bump cluster fallback threshold to route more traffic off similarly aged nodes.

sam (runtime): Canary to 10% held for 5m: p99 for canary streams ~480ms, original path p99 dropped from 2.9s to 1.1s after routing change. Backend 5xxs trending down.

olivia (oncall): Nice. Continue monitoring. Maria, any ETA on replacement node?

maria (infra): We have a warmed spare in us-west-2 pool. If drain completes cleanly, we can decommission gw-node-07 and swap in spare within ~25 minutes.

asha (eng-runtime): Also enabling aggressive KV prefix caching for streaming sessions as a temporary measure. This should reduce device_sync frequency.

leo (sre): Quick snippet to check for repeated stalls in logs: 
```
# find streams with >3 stall events in last 15m
grep -R "send_chunk.*blocked" /var/log/streams | awk '{print $1,$6}' | sort | uniq -c | sort -nr | head
```

sam (runtime): Running that; found 18 sessions tied to gw-node-07. We'll invalidate their caches and let them reconnect to distribute load.

olivia (oncall): Customer impact status update for incident page: 12 customers degraded, 3 had transient 5xx spikes, no data loss. Post-incident action: hardware RMA for gw-node-07, firmware update on same fleet, add automated thermal/fan alarm.

jordan (prod): Starting customer messages: short note explaining degraded latency for streaming, mitigation steps taken, ETA for full recovery once node swap completes.

incident-bot: Auto-create incident ticket INC-TKT-2298765 in Jira and attach logs.

maria (infra): Drain complete. Evicted pods moved to other nodes. Power-cycling gw-node-07 to collect hardware logs before RMA.

sam (runtime): After drain, cluster p99 normalized to ~520ms cluster-wide. 5xx back to baseline. Canary promoted to 100% for affected routes to keep distributed load away from older nodes.

olivia (oncall): Good runbook note: mark gw-node-07 as `do-not-schedule`, RMA if ECC correctables don't reset after reboot.

leo (sre): Follow-ups: 1) RCA for root cause (ECC + thermal + possible firmware). 2) Fleet sweep for similar firmware version. 3) Alert tuning to correlate ECC correctables with streaming stalls. 4) Update playbook with `drain -> fallback routing -> spin spare` sequence.

asha (eng-runtime): Adding an eval job to reproduce stall under synthetic ECC noise (simulated) to confirm model/kernel sensitivity.

jordan (prod): CS notified customers. No escalations.

olivia (oncall): Wrapping up this thread. Will handoff to oncall rotation document for next steps and RCA owners: Maria(root cause + RMA), Sam(telemetry & mitigation), Leo(alerting/playbook), Asha(repro). Closing paging. :white_check_mark:

incident-bot: Incident INC-2298765 acknowledged resolved from paging perspective. Leave the Jira ticket open for RCA and action items.

sam (runtime): Adding logs and timing charts to the Jira ticket.

maria (infra): Uploading hardware dump and nvram logs to ticket.

leo (sre): Will draft postmortem template and timeline.

olivia (oncall): Thanks team. Monitoring for next 30m then switch to watch-only.

incident-bot: This thread archived automatically in 7 days unless re-opened.
